content: Fostemsavir has been associated with QTc interval prolongation, particularly when administered at doses higher than recommended. This effect is observed when fostemsavir is co-administered with other drugs that also prolong the QTc interval, such as haloperidol, hydroxychloroquine sulfate, hydroxyzine, ibutilide, iloperidone, indacaterol (inhaled), inotuzumab, isoflurane, itraconazole, ivosidenib, lapatinib, ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, lefamulin, leflunomide, lenacapavir, lenvatinib, letromovir, leuprolide, levalbuterol, levofloxacin, lithium, lofexidine, loperamide, lopinavir, lumefantrine, macimorelin, mefloquine, midostaurin, mifepristone, mirtazapine, moxifloxacin, nilotinib, nortriptyline, ofloxacin, olanzapine, olodaterol (inhaled), ondansetron, osilodrostat, osimertinib, oxaliplatin, oxytocin, paliperidone, panobinostat, pasireotide, pazopanib, pentamidine, pimavanserin, pimozide, pitolisant, primaquine, procainamide, propafenone, propofol, quetiapine, quinidine, quinine, quizartinib, ranolazine, and others. Caution and close monitoring are advised when fostemsavir is used in combination with these agents, as the risk of QTc prolongation and associated adverse events may increase. Fostemsavir also inhibits OATP1B1/3 and BCRP transporters, which can lead to increased plasma concentrations of drugs that are substrates of these transporters. Examples include imatinib, irinotecan, irinotecan liposomal, lapatinib, ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, leflunomide, lenvatinib, letromovir, lovastatin, methotrexate, mitoxantrone, nitrofurantoin, olmesartan, ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir & dasabuvir (DSC), pantoprazole, pazopanib, penicillin G aqueous, pitavastatin, pravastatin, repaglinide, revefenacin, and others. Therapy modification or dose adjustment is recommended, and co-administration should be avoided if possible. Lenacapavir, which affects hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism, may increase fostemsavir levels and the levels of other CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. This interaction may elevate the risk of adverse reactions associated with CYP3A4 substrates. For statins, fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of pitavastatin, pravastatin, and lovastatin. It is recommended to use the lowest possible starting dose of statins and monitor for associated adverse events. Patients receiving fostemsavir in combination with QTc-prolonging drugs should undergo more frequent ECG monitoring to assess for potential cardiac effects.
